postimage_derivation.why: The digests recorded at 06:2xZ were for the 19-edit table. Round 10 added the two guard edits (G8/B9), so they no longer describe the post-image. They cannot be recomputed until the (ii) placeholder is resolved, which needs NW-01 to have run.
postimage_derivation.append_status_manifest_note: Its four edits are untouched by round 10, so 84dee7d4... will reappear unchanged when the table is re-derived. Recorded here as a prediction to be checked, not carried forward as a pin.

live_measurements_2026_09_12.two_distinct_event_tables: clued_control.execution_events is what read_execution()->'events' returns and what the series_e / budget_sequence segments range over: 88 rows, max sequence 88. clued_control.events is the ROOT event table that read_root()->'events' returns: 5 rows. The root6 GENERATION_REGISTERED event goes into the latter, becoming root event 6 -- it never touches execution_events. An earlier draft of this note said sequence 89 would be the registration event; that was wrong about which table, and is corrected here.
live_measurements_2026_09_12.what_will_occupy_execution_event_89: the twentieth binding forward (runbook step 14), operation EXECUTION_BINDING_FORWARD_ACCEPTED. The new budget lands at 90, following the 84-forward/85-budget pattern of the previous cycle.
live_measurements_2026_09_12.why_the_89_boundary_is_safe: Both 89 and 90 are >= 89, so the new root6 segment catches the budget wherever it lands. The forward event at 89 is never examined by these segments at all: reserve_gate:52 iterates only events whose operation is BUDGET_RESERVED, and reserve_gate:70 iterates attempts. The narrowed segment >=64 and <89 still covers every existing root5-era budget, the highest being 85.
live_measurements_2026_09_12.controller_agreement: context.mjs:152 sets root6BudgetSequence=89 and generationForBudget(s)= s>=89 ? root6, so a budget at 90 resolves to root6 on both sides.

edits.unreachable_reason: reserve_gate:110 reads `if 'GATE'='BUDGET' then` — a constant-false test in the GATE instantiation of this shared template, so lines 111-113 never execute here. The identical line is live in reserve_execution_budget (B7), where :115 reads `if 'BUDGET'='BUDGET' then`. This edit is made to keep the two instantiations byte-comparable, NOT because it has any runtime effect in reserve_gate. ControlPlaneChangeScope.md section 7 listed reserve_gate #7 and reserve_execution_budget #7 as equivalent substantive edits; that was wrong and is corrected here.

edits.adjudication: SuccessorReviewerRound10.md section 8 rules (e). The implementer had preferred (c); the reviewer rejected it because (c)'s second SECURITY DEFINER replacement lands inside the runbook's irreversible zone and because its expected value would be self-read by the reviewed party after its own write instead of being auditable in advance. The implementer accepts both reasons.
edits.what: Replaces the one already-failing whole-root digest guard with three assertions, all computable before any write: (i) the five frozen historical events byte-for-byte including recorded_at, (ii) every other root key plus the registration event with only recorded_at removed, (iii) the event count is exactly 6 so nothing can be appended outside the digest domain. The exception name is unchanged and no raise is removed.
edits.why_that_costs_no_strength: It is written by clock_timestamp(), so no caller can set it; append_event already pins clock_timestamp() inside [not_before, expires_at); and events_immutable forbids UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE afterwards.
edits.placeholder_resolution: Computed by work/cp01/derive-projected-root-digest.sql AFTER NW-01 (runbook step 8) and BEFORE CP-01 (step 9), with a read-only SQL that builds the projection in-database. Never with JS-side serialisation: jsonb key order is Postgres's, not insertion order and not lexicographic (R9-F1).
